verses.text: Na di words of di Preacher, David pikin, wey be king for Jerusalem.
“Vanity of vanities,” di Preacher talk, “vanity of vanities! Everything na vanity.”
Wetin person dey gain from all im hard work wey e dey do under di sun?
One generation dey go and another generation dey come, but di earth dey stand forever.
Di sun dey rise and di sun dey set, and e dey hurry go back to di place wey e dey rise.
Di wind dey blow go south, and e dey turn go north. E dey turn round and round as e dey go, and di wind dey return to im circuit.
All di rivers dey run enter di sea, yet di sea no dey full. To di place wey di rivers dey come from, na there dem dey return go.
All things dey tire person pass wetin person fit talk. Di eye no dey satisfy with seeing, and di ear no dey full with hearing.
Wetin don happen before na im go happen again, and wetin dem don do before na im dem go do again. Nothing new dey under di sun.
Anything dey wey person fit point at and talk say, “See, dis one new”? E don dey before, for di ages wey pass before us.
Nobody dey remember di people of before, and di people wey go come after no go remember dem too, even among those wey go come later.
I, di Preacher, na king over Israel for Jerusalem.
I give my heart to seek and to search out wisdom concerning all wetin dey happen under heaven. Na heavy work God don give di human pikin dem to dey busy with.
I don see all di works wey dem dey do under di sun, and see, all of dem na vanity and chasing wind.
Wetin crooked no fit straight, and wetin dey lack no fit count.
I talk with my own heart say, “See, I don become great and I don gather more wisdom pass all wey dey Jerusalem before me. Yes, my heart don experience plenty wisdom and knowledge.”
I give my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and foolishness. I know say dis one too na chasing wind.
Because plenty wisdom dey with plenty sorrow, and di person wey increase knowledge dey increase pain.
I talk for my heart say, “Come now, I go test you with joy. Enjoy pleasure.” See, dis one too na vanity.
I talk about laughter say, “E dey mad,” and about joy say, “Wetin e dey do?”

I search with my heart how to cheer my body with wine, my heart still dey guide me with wisdom, and how to hold foolishness, until I see wetin good for di human pikin dem to do under heaven all di days of dem life.
I do great works. I build house dem for myself. I plant vineyards for myself.
I make gardens and parks for myself, and I plant for dem all kinds of fruit tree.
I make pools of water for myself, to water di forest wey dey grow trees.
I get male servants and female servants, and I get servants wey dem born for my house. I also get plenty cattle, herds and flocks, pass all wey dey Jerusalem before me.
I gather silver and gold for myself, and di treasure of kings and of di provinces. I get men singers and women singers for myself, and di delights of di human pikin dem, many concubines.
So I become great, and I increase pass all wey dey Jerusalem before me. My wisdom still dey with me.
Anything wey my eyes want, I no hold am back from dem. I no stop my heart from any joy, because my heart enjoy all my work, and dis na my reward for all my work.
Den I look all di works wey my hands don do, and di hard work wey I labour to do. See, everything na vanity and chasing wind, and no profit dey under di sun.
I turn myself to see wisdom, madness and foolishness. Wetin di man wey dey come after di king go do? Only wetin dem don do before.
Den I see say wisdom better pass foolishness, as light better pass darkness.
Di wise man eyes dey im head, but di fool dey waka for darkness. I still see say di same thing dey happen to dem both.
Den I talk for my heart say, “Wetin happen to di fool go happen to me too. Why den I don dey wise pass?” Den I talk for my heart say dis one too na vanity.
Because dem no go remember di wise man pass di fool forever, since for di days wey dey come everything don dey forgotten. Di wise man dey die like di fool!
So I hate life, because di work wey dem dey do under di sun dey grieve me, because everything na vanity and chasing wind.
I hate all my hard work wey I work under di sun, because I must leave am for di man wey go come after me.
Who know whether e go be wise man or fool? Yet e go rule over all my work wey I labour for and use wisdom do under di sun. Dis one too na vanity.
So I turn go despair for my heart over all di hard work wey I work under di sun.
Because person dey wey im work dey with wisdom, knowledge and skill, yet e must leave am as im share to person wey no work for am. Dis one too na vanity and big evil.
Because wetin person get from all im hard work, and from di striving of im heart, wey e dey work hard for under di sun?
Because all im days na sorrows, and im work na grief. Even for night, im heart no dey rest. Dis one too na vanity.
Nothing better dey for person than say e eat and drink, and make im soul enjoy good for im work. Dis one too, I see say e dey from God hand.
Because who fit eat, or who fit enjoy, more than me?

Because to di man wey good for im sight, God dey give wisdom, knowledge and joy; but to di sinner, e dey give di work to gather and to heap up, so that e go give am to di one wey good for God sight. Dis one too na vanity and chasing wind.
Everything get im season, and every purpose under heaven get im time:
time to born and time to die; time to plant and time to pluck wetin dem plant;
time to kill and time to heal; time to break down and time to build up;
time to cry and time to laugh; time to mourn and time to dance;
time to throw stones away and time to gather stones together; time to embrace and time to refuse to embrace;
time to seek and time to lose; time to keep and time to throw away;
time to tear and time to sew; time to keep quiet and time to talk;
time to love and time to hate; time for war and time for peace.
Wetin di worker dey gain from di work wey e dey labour for?
I don see di burden wey God don give di human pikin dem to dey busy with.
E don make everything fine for im time. Also, e don put eternity inside dem heart, yet nobody fit understand di work wey God don do from beginning to end.
I know say nothing better dey for dem than to rejoice and to do good as dem dey live.
Also, make every man eat and drink and enjoy good for all im work. Dis na God gift.
I know say everything wey God do go last forever. Nothing fit add to am, and nothing fit comot from am. God don do am so that people go fear am.
Wetin dey now don dey before, and wetin go come don dey before, and God dey seek again wetin don pass.
Moreover, I see under di sun, for di place of judgment, wickedness dey there, and for di place of righteousness, wickedness dey there.
I talk for my heart say, “God go judge di righteous and di wicked, because time dey for every purpose and for every work.”
I talk for my heart say, “As for di human pikin dem, God dey test dem so that dem go see say dem be like animals.”

Because wetin happen to di human pikin dem happen to di animals. Di same thing dey happen to dem. As di one die, so di other die. Yes, dem all get di same breath, and man no get advantage over di animal, because everything na vanity.
Dem all dey go di same place. Dem all come from di dust, and dem all dey return to di dust.
Who know whether di spirit of man dey go up, and di spirit of di animal dey go down to di earth?
So I see say nothing better dey than say man rejoice for im works, because na im share be dis. Who go bring am to see wetin go happen after am?

Again I look and see all di oppression wey dey happen under di sun. See, di tears of di people wey dem oppress, and dem no get person wey go comfort dem. Power dey di hand of dem oppressors, and dem no get person wey go comfort dem.
So I praise di dead wey don die before, pass di living wey still dey alive.
Yes, better pass dem both na di one wey never born, wey never see di evil work wey dem dey do under di sun.
Den I see all di hard work and all di skill for work, say na from man envy of im neighbour e come. Dis one too na vanity and chasing wind.
Di fool dey fold im hands and dey eat im own flesh.
Better handful with quietness, than two handfuls with hard work and chasing wind.
Den I turn again and see vanity under di sun.

Man dey wey dey alone, e no get second person. Yes, e no get pikin or brother. Yet no end dey to im hard work, and im eyes no dey satisfy with riches. “For who den I dey work hard and dey deny myself good things?” Dis one too na vanity, yes, na painful work.
Two better pass one, because dem get good reward for dem work.
Because if dem fall, one go lift im friend up. But sorrow dey for di one wey fall when e dey alone, because e no get another person to help am up.
Again, if two lie down together, dem go dey warm, but how one person alone go dey warm?
If person fit overpower one person alone, two go stand against am. Di cord wey three strands twist no dey quickly break.
Better na poor and wise young man pass old and foolish king wey no know how to take warning again.
Because from prison e come out to reign; yes, even for im kingdom e born as poor man.
I see all di living wey dey waka under di sun, with di second young man wey go stand for di king place.
Dere no dey end to all di people, to all wey e dey lead. Yet dem wey go come after no go rejoice for am. Surely dis one too na vanity and chasing wind.
Guard your steps as you dey go di house of God; to draw near to listen better pass to give di sacrifice of fools, because dem no know say dem dey do evil.
No rush with your mouth, and make your heart no hurry to talk anything before God, because God dey heaven and you dey earth. So make your words dey few.
Because dream dey come with plenty business, and fool voice dey come with plenty words.
When you make vow to God, no delay to pay am, because e no dey happy with fools. Pay wetin you don vow.
Better say you no vow pass say you vow and no pay.
No allow your mouth cause your body to sin. No talk before di messenger say na mistake. Why make God vex with your voice and destroy di work of your hands?
Because plenty dreams and plenty words dey with vanity. But you must fear God.

If you see oppression of di poor, and di violent wey dem dey take away justice and righteousness for di province, no marvel at di matter, because one official dey above another official, and higher ones dey above dem.
Again, di profit of di earth dey for all; even di king dey get profit from di field.
Di person wey love silver no go satisfy with silver, nor di person wey love wealth with im increase. Dis one too na vanity.
When goods increase, dem wey dey eat dem increase. Wetin good dey for di owner, except to look dem with im eyes?
Di sleep of labourer dey sweet, whether e eat small or plenty, but di fullness of di rich man no go allow am sleep.
Dere dey one grievous evil wey I don see under di sun: riches wey owner keep to im own harm.
Dose riches dey perish by bad business, and if e born pikin, nothing dey im hand.
As e come out of im mama womb, naked e go go back as e come, and e no go carry anything from im labour wey e fit carry for im hand.
Dis one too na grievous evil: exactly as e come, so e go go. Wetin profit e get wey labour for di wind?
All im days e dey eat for darkness, with plenty vexation, sickness and anger.
See wetin I don see: na good and fitting say man eat and drink, and enjoy good for all im labour wey e dey labour under di sun, all di days of im life wey God give am, because na im share be dat.
Also every man wey God don give riches and wealth, and don give am power to eat from dem, to receive im share and to rejoice for im labour, dis na God gift.
Because e no go remember di days of im life much, because God dey answer am with di joy of im heart.
Dere dey one evil wey I don see under di sun, and e dey heavy upon men:
a man wey God give riches, wealth and honour, so that im soul no lack anything wey e desire, yet God no give am power to enjoy am, but stranger dey enjoy am. Dis na vanity, and na evil sickness.
If man born 100 pikin and live many years, so that di days of im years plenty, but im soul no get satisfaction with good, and e no even get burial, I talk say di untimely birth better pass am.
Because e come in vanity and e go for darkness, and im name go cover with darkness.
Also e no see di sun nor know anything. E get more rest pass di other man.
Yes, even if e live twice 1,000 years, yet no enjoy good, no be to one place all dey go?
All di labour of man na for im mouth, and still di appetite no dey satisfy.
Because wetin di wise man get more pass di fool? Wetin di poor man get, wey know how to waka before di living?
Di sight of di eyes better pass di wandering of desire. Dis one too na vanity and chasing wind.
Wetin dey don get im name, and e don known say na man; e no fit contend with wetin strong pass am.
Seeing say plenty words dey wey increase vanity, wetin man profit?
Because who know wetin good for man for dis life, all di days of im vain life wey dey pass like shadow? Because who fit tell man wetin go happen after am under di sun?
Good name better pass fine perfume, and di day of death pass di day of birth.
E better to go to di house of mourning pass to go to di house of feasting, because dat na di end of all men, and di living go take am to heart.
Sorrow better pass laughter, because by sad face di heart dey made better.
Di heart of di wise dey di house of mourning, but di heart of fools dey di house of mirth.
E better to hear di rebuke of di wise pass to hear di song of fools.
Because as di crackling of thorns under pot, so be di laughter of di fool. Dis one too na vanity.
Surely oppression dey make di wise man mad, and bribe dey destroy di heart.
Di end of one thing better pass im beginning. Di patient in spirit better pass di proud in spirit.
No rush for your spirit to dey angry, because anger dey rest for di chest of fools.
No talk say, “Why di former days better pass dis one?” because you no dey ask dis one with wisdom.
Wisdom good with inheritance, yes, e dey profit those wey see di sun.
Because wisdom na shelter, even as money na shelter; but di excellence of knowledge be say wisdom dey preserve di life of am wey get am.
Consider di work of God, because who fit make straight wetin e don make crooked?
For di day of prosperity, dey joyful, and for di day of adversity, consider. Yes, God don make di one as di other, so that man no go find out anything wey go come after am.
I don see all dis for my days of vanity: dere dey righteous man wey dey perish for im righteousness, and dere dey wicked man wey dey prolong im life for im wickedness.
No be righteous too much, nor make yourself too wise. Why you go destroy yourself?
No be wicked too much, nor be foolish. Why you go die before your time?
E good say you hold dis one, yes, also no take your hand from dat one, because di one wey fear God go come out with dem all.
Wisdom dey strengthen di wise man more pass ten rulers wey dey di city.
Surely no righteous man dey for di earth wey dey do good and no dey sin.
Also no take heed to all words wey dem talk, so that you no go hear your servant dey curse you,
because many times your own heart know say you too don curse others.
All dis I don prove with wisdom. I talk say, “I go be wise,” but e dey far from me.
Wetin dey far off and deep, deep, who fit find am out?
I turn my heart to know and to search out and to seek wisdom and di reason of things, and to know di wickedness of folly, and di foolishness wey be madness.
I find something more bitter pass death: di woman wey im heart na snares and nets, and im hands na chains. Di one wey please God go escape from am, but di sinner go dey caught by am.
“See, I don find dis,” di Preacher talk, “as I dey add one thing to another to find di conclusion;
wey my soul still dey seek but I no find. I don find one man among 1,000, but I no find woman among all dem.”
See, only dis I don find: say God make man upright, but dem don seek many schemes.
Who be like di wise man? And who know di interpretation of a thing? Man wisdom dey make im face shine, and di hardness of im face dey change.
I talk say, keep di king command, and dat na because of di oath of God.
No rush to go from im presence. No stand for evil thing, because e dey do whatever e like.
Because di king word get power, and who fit talk to am say, “Wetin you dey do?”
Whoever keep di command no go know any evil thing, and di wise man heart dey discern di time and di way.
Because for every purpose dey time and way, because di misery of man dey heavy upon am.
Because e no know wetin go happen, because who fit tell am how e go happen?
No man get power over di spirit to keep di spirit, and e no get power over di day of death. Dere no discharge for dat war, and wickedness no go deliver dem wey dey give demselves to am.
All dis I don see, and apply my heart to every work wey dem dey do under di sun, wey one man dey rule over another to im own hurt.
So I see di wicked buried, wey come and go from di holy place, and dem forget dem for di city wey dem do so. Dis one too na vanity.
Because sentence against evil work no dey quickly executed, di heart of di human pikin dem dey fully set for dem to do evil.
Though sinner do evil 100 times and prolong im days, yet I know say e go dey well with dem wey fear God, wey fear before am;
but e no go dey well with di wicked, neither e go prolong im days like shadow, because e no fear before God.

Dere dey vanity wey dey happen on earth: say dere dey righteous men wey e dey happen to dem according to di work of di wicked; again, dere dey wicked men wey e dey happen to dem according to di work of di righteous. I talk say dis one too na vanity.
Den I commend mirth, because man no get better thing under di sun than to eat, drink and be merry, and dat dey go with am for im labour all di days of im life wey God give am under di sun.
When I apply my heart to know wisdom and to see di business wey dey happen on earth (even day or night, e no dey see sleep with im eyes),

den I see all di work of God, say man no fit find out di work wey dey happen under di sun. However man labour to seek am, e no go find am. Yes, even if di wise man think say e go know am, e no fit find am.
Because all dis I consider in my heart, to explain am all: say di righteous, di wise, and dem works dey God hand. Man no know either love or hatred; all dey before dem.

All things dey come alike to all. Di same event dey happen to di righteous and to di wicked; to di good, to di clean and to di unclean; to di one wey dey sacrifice and to di one wey no dey sacrifice. As di good man, so di sinner; di one wey swear, as di one wey fear to swear.

Dis na evil for all wey dey happen under di sun, say di same event dey happen to all. Yes, also di heart of di human pikin dem full of evil, and madness dey dem heart while dem dey live, and after dat dem go join di dead.
Because for am wey dem join to all di living dere dey hope, for living dog better pass dead lion.
Because di living know say dem go die, but di dead no know anything, neither dem get any more reward, because di memory of dem don forgotten.
Also dem love, dem hatred and dem envy don perish, neither dem get any more portion forever for anything wey dey happen under di sun.
Go your way. Eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with merry heart, because God don already accept your works.
Make your garments dey white always, and make your head no lack oil.

Live joyfully with di wife wey you love all di days of di life of your vanity, wey e don give you under di sun, all di days of your vanity, because dat na your portion for life and for your labour wey you labour under di sun.
Whatever your hand find to do, do am with your might, because dere no dey work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, for Sheol, wia you dey go.

I return and see under di sun say di race no dey for di swift, nor di battle for di strong, neither bread for di wise, nor riches for men of understanding, nor favour for men of skill; but time and chance dey happen to dem all.
Because man no know im time. As fish wey dem catch for evil net, and as birds wey dem catch for snare, so di human pikin dem dey trapped for evil time, when e fall suddenly upon dem.
I don also see dis wisdom under di sun, and e great to me:
dere dey small city, and few men inside am, and one great king come against am, besiege am and build great siege works against am.
Now dere dey find inside am one poor wise man, and e deliver di city by im wisdom. Yet nobody remember dat same poor man.
Den I talk say, “Wisdom better pass strength.” Nevertheless di poor man wisdom dem despise, and dem no hear im words.
Di words of di wise wey dem hear quietly better pass di shout of am wey rule among fools.
Wisdom better pass weapons of war, but one sinner dey destroy plenty good.
Dead flies dey make di perfumer ointment stink and send forth stinking odour. So small folly dey outweigh wisdom and honour.
Di wise man heart dey im right hand, but di fool heart dey im left.
Yes also, when di fool dey waka for di way, im understanding dey fail am, and e dey show to everyone say e na fool.
If di ruler spirit rise against you, no leave your place, because calmness dey lay great offences to rest.
Dere dey evil wey I don see under di sun, like error wey dey proceed from di ruler:
folly dey set for great dignity, and di rich dey sit for low place.
I don see servants upon horses, and princes dey waka like servants upon di earth.
Di one wey dig pit go fall inside am, and di one wey break through wall, serpent go bite am.
Di one wey quarry stones go dey hurt by dem, and di one wey split wood dey endanger by am.
If di iron blunt and one no sharpen di edge, den e must use more strength; but wisdom dey profit to bring success.
If di serpent bite before e dey charmed, den di charmer no dey profit.
Di words of di wise man mouth dey gracious, but di lips of fool dey swallow am up.
Di beginning of di words of im mouth na foolishness, and di end of im talk na wicked madness.
Di fool dey multiply words. Man no know wetin go happen, and wetin go happen after am, who fit tell am?
Di labour of fools dey weary dem, because dem no know how to go to di city.
Trouble dey for you, land, when your king na child, and your princes dey feast for morning!
Blessing dey for you, land, when your king na son of nobles, and your princes dey eat for di right time, for strength and no for drunkenness!
By slothfulness di roof dey sink, and through idleness of hands di house dey leak.
Dem dey make feast for laughter, and wine dey make life merry, and money dey answer all things.
No curse di king, no even for your thought, and no curse di rich for your bedroom, because bird of di sky go carry di voice, and di one wey get wings go tell di matter.
